title: Biomolecular condensate microstructure is invariant to sequence-encoded molecular and macroscopic properties.
authors: Tan, Daniel; Aierken, Dilimulati; Garcia, Pablo L; Joseph, Jerelle A
one_liner_zh: 该文用粗粒化模拟与图论分析揭示LCD凝聚体的小世界网络微结构不随序列变化，建立单分子构象、网络拓扑与宏观材料性质的多尺度关联，直接聚焦无序蛋白相分离中的互作网络机制建模。
abstract: Biomolecular condensates, including those formed by prion-like low complexity domains (LCDs) of proteins, are maintained by networks of molecular interactions. Such collective interactions give rise to the rich array of material behaviors underlying condensate function. Previous work has uncovered distinct LCD conformations in condensates versus dilute phases, and recently, single-component LCD condensates have been predicted to exhibit microstructures with "small-world" networks-where molecular nodes are highly clustered and connected via short pathlengths. However, a framework linking single-molecule properties, condensate microstructure, and macroscopic material properties remains elusive. Here, we combine molecular simulation and graph-theoretic analysis to reveal that small-world microstructures are inherent properties of LCD-like polymers, whose sequence features impact both molecule-scale conformations and droplet-scale material properties while maintaining a stable network structure. Using a residue-resolution coarse-grained model, we probe condensates comprising naturally-occuring LCD sequences and generalize our findings by varying composition and patterning in binary sequences of hydrophobic and polar residues. We show that non-blocky sequences, including a hydrophobic homopolymer, form condensates with small-world internal networks featuring "hubs"-molecules responsible for global connectivity-and "cliques", molecular clusters bound by persistent short-ranged associations. Cliques localize near interfaces without a secondary phase transition, suggesting a role in mediating molecular partitioning and condensate aging by tuning interfacial material properties. Moreover, we discover that network small-worldness and droplet surface tension are consequences of sequence length and hydrophobicity. We also track single-molecule structure and dynamics inside condensates, revealing that internal heterogeneity at the single-molecule level is systematically encoded by network topology. Collectively, our work establishes multiscale structure-property relationships in LCD condensates, elucidating general organizing principles of the condensate microstructure that persist with sequence-driven changes in molecular behaviors and material properties.
abstract_zh: 生物分子凝聚体，包括由蛋白质的朊病毒样低复杂度结构域（LCDs）形成的那些，通过分子相互作用网络得以维持。这种集体相互作用产生了凝聚体功能所依赖的丰富材料行为阵列。先前的研究已揭示凝聚体与稀相中LCD构象的差异，并且最近，单组分LCD凝聚体被预测表现出具有“小世界”网络的微观结构——其中分子节点高度聚集并通过短路径长度相连。然而，一个将单分子性质、凝聚体微观结构和宏观材料性质联系起来的框架仍然难以捉摸。在此，我们结合分子模拟和图论分析，揭示小世界微观结构是LCD样聚合物的固有属性，其序列特征影响分子尺度构象和液滴尺度材料性质，同时维持稳定的网络结构。使用残基分辨率的粗粒化模型，我们探测由天然存在的LCD序列组成的凝聚体，并通过改变疏水性和极性残基二元序列的组成和模式来推广我们的发现。我们表明，非嵌段序列，包括疏水均聚物，形成具有小世界内部网络的凝聚体，该网络包含“枢纽”——负责全局连接的分子——以及“团簇”，即由持久短程关联结合的分子簇。团簇在无次级相变的情况下定位于界面附近，提示其在通过调节界面材料性质介导分子分配和凝聚体老化中的作用。此外，我们发现网络小世界性和液滴表面张力是序列长度和疏水性的结果。我们还追踪凝聚体内单分子结构和动力学，揭示单分子水平的内部异质性由网络拓扑系统编码。总体而言，我们的工作建立了LCD凝聚体中的多尺度结构-性质关系，阐明了凝聚体微观结构的普遍组织原则，这些原则在序列驱动的分子行为和材料性质变化中持续存在。
